headline_marked: [[PM Tarique Rahman's flight delayed by nearly 5 hours]] from Japan due to spoiler glitch
headline: PM Tarique Rahman's flight delayed by nearly 5 hours from Japan due to spoiler glitch
summary: The Biman aircraft carrying the Prime Minister developed a fault in its spoiler system before takeoff at Narita International Airport, causing a significant delay. Engineers deactivated the affected spoiler, allowing the flight to eventually depart for Dhaka.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's return flight from Japan was delayed by nearly five hours yesterday after a Biman aircraft developed a fault in its spoiler system at Narita International Airport. The flight, carrying the PM and his entourage, was scheduled to depart at 3:00 PM Bangladesh time.

The aircraft, a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, began moving towards the runway when a fault was detected in its No. 1 hydraulic spoiler. Spoilers are crucial movable panels on wings that help reduce lift and control aircraft movement.

Engineers quickly worked to deactivate the affected spoiler, a procedure permissible under US Federal Aviation Administration guidelines for the Boeing 787 under specific conditions. This allowed the Prime Minister to return on the same aircraft.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines stated that no defects were found during pre-flight inspections; the fault developed only after the aircraft began taxiing. The flight eventually took off from Narita at 7:55 PM Bangladesh time.

PM Tarique Rahman was returning from a four-day official visit to Japan, from October 26 to 29, at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. His wife, Dr. Zubaida Rahman, and other delegation members were also aboard.

This incident marks another technical issue for Biman aircraft carrying Bangladeshi prime ministers. In 2016, a Biman flight with then-PM Sheikh Hasina made an emergency landing in Turkmenistan due to an engine oil-pressure problem.

headline_marked: [[Awami League leader Mahbubul Alam Hanif sentenced to death]] for crimes against humanity in Kushtia
headline: Awami League leader Mahbubul Alam Hanif sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in Kushtia
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 delivered the verdict for Hanif and three others involved in the killing of six protesters during the July 2024 mass uprising. Three co-convicts received life imprisonment.
details: International Crimes Tribunal-2 yesterday sentenced Awami League Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death. The verdict was for crimes against humanity over the killing of six protesters in Kushtia during the July 2024 mass uprising.

Three other convicts, Awami League Kushtia district and city unit leaders Sadruddin Khan, Azgar Ali and Ataur Rahman Ata, were sentenced to imprisonment for the remainder of their natural lives. They were also involved in the killings.

The three-member tribunal, headed by Chairman Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, delivered the verdict over the killings on August 5, 2024. This was the day the Sheikh Hasina-led government fell amid the student-led uprising.

The tribunal also ordered the confiscation of half of each convict’s immovable property. Proceeds from the sale will be distributed as compensation to the families of those killed and injured through the July Foundation or another designated statutory body.

The prosecution initially brought three charges, but the tribunal framed five. These charges covered murder, torture, persecution, conspiracy to suppress the movement with lethal force, and a common criminal design to attack civilians.

The tribunal also sentenced all four to rigorous life imprisonment under the remaining charges. Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam welcomed the verdict as a mark of respect to the souls of those martyred during the July Uprising.

Yesterday’s judgment was the eighth delivered by ICT-1 and ICT-2 since their reconstitution following the political changeover on August 5, 2024. The tribunals have so far convicted 72 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, and 23 have been sentenced to death.

The investigation for this case began on March 25, 2025, with the prosecution pressing charges on September 11. The tribunal framed charges on November 2, and arguments concluded on October 7, after which the case was kept pending for verdict.
